summary.headline: ASR, security baseline, and Recovery Lock guidance are updated
summary.overview: The day refreshes endpoint-security ASR policy, security-baseline configuration, Settings catalog Recovery Lock, EPM roadmap, and Configuration Manager LTSB reference material.
summary.adminImpact: Review current ASR and baseline documentation before policy changes, and validate Recovery Lock configuration through Settings catalog with appropriate operational recovery procedures.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint security ASR policy guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The ASR policy reference receives a substantive update and remains the current source for configuring attack-surface-reduction controls in Intune.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock configuration guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The Settings catalog Recovery Lock guide is refreshed, supporting current configuration and recovery planning for eligible devices.

summary.headline: March Intune roadmap is announced
summary.overview: The March In Development roadmap is the material change, alongside small updates to in-development content and iOS/iPadOS line-of-business app guidance.
summary.adminImpact: Review the March roadmap with change owners and support teams, then update user communications and test plans before upcoming features reach the tenant.

keyChanges.title: March 2026 Intune In Development roadmap is available
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announces the March upcoming-feature list for organizational readiness and future-release planning.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS line-of-business app guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The LOB app deployment reference receives maintenance updates, retaining the current setup documentation.

summary.headline: Windows Autopatch will enable Hotpatch by default for eligible devices
summary.overview: A Message Center plan announces that Windows Autopatch will enable Hotpatch security updates by default from May 2026 for eligible Intune devices; device-profile troubleshooting and LTSB documentation are also updated.
summary.adminImpact: Determine which eligible Autopatch devices should remain on Hotpatch and which require opt-out when that control becomes available in April. Validate prerequisites such as VBS now, and prepare help-desk messaging around changed restart behavior.

keyChanges.title: Autopatch Hotpatch becomes default for eligible devices in May
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopatch plans to enable Hotpatch security updates by default beginning May 2026. Eligible devices receive security updates with fewer restarts; an opt-out is planned for April and VBS is among the stated prerequisites.

summary.headline: Endpoint-security settings references receive a broad Windows policy refresh
summary.overview: Forty-seven changes refresh antivirus, firewall, ASR, EDR, Configuration Manager tenant-attach firewall, and related Windows endpoint-security guidance.
summary.adminImpact: Use the current setting references when reviewing policy baselines or migrating Configuration Manager-managed firewall settings to Intune. Confirm tenant-attach scope before applying Intune endpoint-security firewall policy to Configuration Manager devices.

keyChanges.title: Windows Security experience antivirus settings are updated
keyChanges.detail: The antivirus policy-settings reference receives a substantial update, keeping current Windows Security experience configuration information available.

keyChanges.title: Tenant-attach firewall settings guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The reference for using Intune endpoint-security firewall settings with Configuration Manager devices is refreshed, supporting co-management policy planning.

summary.headline: Security policy maintenance and Autopatch Hotpatch readiness dominate the week
summary.overview: The week records 82 changes, including major refreshes to ASR, antivirus, EDR, firewall, and baseline references. Two Message Center notices publish the March roadmap and the May default enablement of Autopatch Hotpatch.
summary.adminImpact: Start Hotpatch readiness and opt-out decisions now, review endpoints for VBS and eligibility, and update ASR, firewall, EDR, and antivirus runbooks from the refreshed references. Include the March roadmap in change-planning cadence.

keyChanges.title: Autopatch plans Hotpatch as the eligible-device default
keyChanges.detail: From May 2026, Autopatch will enable Hotpatch by default for eligible devices; administrators gain an opt-out in April and should validate prerequisites including VBS.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint-security policy references are comprehensively refreshed
keyChanges.detail: ASR, antivirus, EDR, firewall, and tenant-attach firewall setting guidance are updated across the week.

keyChanges.title: March In Development roadmap is published
keyChanges.detail: The roadmap provides the current upcoming-feature list for organizational readiness planning.
